description.summary: manage foreign toplevel windows

protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol allows privileged clients such as dock or taskbar components to observe and manage toplevel windows on behalf of the compositor. It provides access to window metadata (title, app-id, state, parent, outputs), allows requests to maximize, minimize, activate, close, or fullscreen a toplevel, and supports a dock preview context for thumbnail display and tooltip overlays.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", "may", and "recommended" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2

description.summary: observe and manage toplevel windows

interface.description:
A singleton global that emits one treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 object per mapped toplevel window. Clients bind this global to receive the toplevel event stream and to create dock preview contexts.
A toplevel is defined as a surface with a role similar to xdg_toplevel. XWayland surfaces may be treated like toplevels in this protocol.
Clients which only care about the current state can perform a roundtrip after binding this global.
The typical lifecycle is: 1. Client binds treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2. 2. Compositor emits a toplevel event for each already-mapped toplevel, followed by individual property events and a done event on each handle. 3. As windows appear and disappear the compositor emits further toplevel events and closed events on the corresponding handles. 4. When the client no longer needs the manager it sends stop, waits for the finished event, destroys the handles, and then the manager itself. Outstanding handles remain usable until the client destroys them individually.

enum.name: error

description.summary: protocol errors for this interface

enum.description: Error values raised as protocol errors on misuse of treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2 requests.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the relative_surface passed to get_dock_preview_context is not a valid wl_surface owned by the calling client

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the manager object

request.description:
This request should be called either when the client will no longer use the manager, or after the finished event has been received.
If a client wishes to destroy this object it should send a stop request and wait for a finished event, then destroy the handles and then this object.
Existing treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 objects created through this manager are not affected and must be destroyed separately by the client.

request.name: stop

description.summary: stop sending events

request.description:
This request indicates that the client no longer wishes to receive events for new toplevels.
The Wayland protocol is asynchronous, meaning the compositor may send further toplevel events until the stop request is processed. The client should wait for a finished event before destroying this object.

request.name: get_dock_preview_context

description.summary: create a dock preview context for a surface

request.description:
Create a treeland_dock_preview_context_v2 associated with the given surface. The surface must be a valid wl_surface owned by the calling client and serves as the anchor for all preview and tooltip positioning.
Only one dock preview context may be active per surface at a time. If a new context is created for a surface that already has one, the compositor destroys the previous context.
The context is destroyed by calling treeland_dock_preview_context_v2.destroy.

arg.name: relative_surface
arg.summary: anchor surface for preview and tooltip positioning

arg.name: id
arg.summary: the new dock preview context object

event.name: toplevel

description.summary: a toplevel window has been mapped

event.description:
Emitted by the compositor whenever a new toplevel window is mapped. The event is sent for all toplevels regardless of which application created them.
Immediately after this event the compositor will send the initial property events (title, app_id, pid, identifier, state, output_enter, parent, and so on) on the new handle, followed by a done event. The client should treat all property events received before the first done as the initial snapshot.

arg.name: toplevel
arg.summary: the new toplevel handle

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor has finished with the toplevel manager

event.description:
This event indicates that the compositor is done sending events to this object. The client should destroy the object. See treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2.destroy for more information.
The compositor must not send any more toplevel events after this event.
Outstanding treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 objects are not affected by this event.

interface.name: treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2

description.summary: handle for a foreign toplevel window

interface.description:
Represents a single mapped toplevel window. The compositor creates this object in response to the manager's toplevel event and destroys the server-side resource when the window is unmapped (signalled by the closed event).
After the compositor sends closed, the client must not send any requests other than destroy. The client should call destroy promptly after receiving closed to release compositor-side tracking state.
All property events (title, app_id, pid, identifier, output_enter, output_leave, state, parent) are grouped by a trailing done event so that a batch of related changes appears atomic to the client.

enum.name: state

description.summary: toplevel window state flags

enum.description: Flags that describe the current state of a toplevel window. These correspond to the states with the same names defined in the xdg-toplevel interface. Each flag is encoded as a uint32 value in the array sent by the state event.

entry.name: attention
entry.summary: the toplevel is requesting user attention

enum.name: error

description.summary: protocol errors for this interface

enum.description: Error values raised as protocol errors on misuse of treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 requests.

entry.name: invalid_geometry
entry.summary: the provided set_icon_geometry dimensions are invalid

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the handle object

request.description:
Destroy the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 object and release all associated client-side resources.
This request may be sent at any time, including before the compositor sends the closed event. When sent after closed, it finalizes the destruction sequence initiated by the compositor. When sent before closed, the compositor will silently drop any further events for this handle.
When a handle is destroyed, a new handle may not be created by the compositor until the toplevel is unmapped and then remapped. Destroying a toplevel handle is not recommended unless the client is cleaning up child objects before destroying the manager, the toplevel was closed, or the handle will not be used in the future.
Other protocols which extend the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 interface should require destructors for extension interfaces to be called before allowing the toplevel handle to be destroyed.

request.name: set_maximized

description.summary: request that the toplevel be maximized

request.description: Request that the compositor maximize the toplevel. The compositor may ignore the request. If the maximized state changes, the compositor will reflect this in a subsequent state event followed by done.

request.name: unset_maximized

description.summary: request that the toplevel be unmaximized

request.description: Request that the compositor restore the toplevel from the maximized state. The compositor may ignore the request. If the state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.

request.name: set_minimized

description.summary: request that the toplevel be minimized

request.description: Request that the compositor minimize the toplevel. The compositor may ignore the request. If the minimized state changes, the compositor will reflect this in a subsequent state event followed by done.

request.name: unset_minimized

description.summary: request that the toplevel be unminimized

request.description: Request that the compositor restore the toplevel from the minimized state. The compositor may ignore the request. If the state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.

request.name: set_fullscreen

description.summary: request that the toplevel enter fullscreen

request.description:
Request that the compositor fullscreen the toplevel on the given output. If output is null, the compositor chooses the output. The output argument is a hint only; the compositor may fullscreen on a different output or not at all.
If the fullscreen state or visible outputs change, the compositor will reflect this via state and output_enter / output_leave events followed by done.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: preferred output for fullscreen, or null for compositor choice

request.name: unset_fullscreen

description.summary: request that the toplevel leave fullscreen

request.description: Request that the compositor exit the fullscreen state for the toplevel. The compositor may ignore the request. If the state changes, it is reflected via state and done events.

request.name: activate

description.summary: request that the toplevel be activated

request.description: Request that the compositor give keyboard focus to the toplevel on the given seat. There is no guarantee the toplevel will actually be activated; the compositor may ignore the request based on seat focus policy or security considerations.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: the seat on which to activate the toplevel

request.name: close

description.summary: request that the toplevel close itself

request.description: Send a close request to the toplevel. The compositor typically forwards this to the application using a shell-specific mechanism such as xdg_toplevel.close. There is no guarantee the application will honour the request. If the toplevel is eventually unmapped, the compositor will emit the closed event on this handle.

request.name: set_icon_geometry

description.summary: set the icon geometry of the toplevel

request.description:
Inform the compositor of the rectangle on surface that visually represents this toplevel (for example the taskbar icon or thumbnail), similar to the EWMH _NET_WM_ICON_GEOMETRY property. The compositor may use this as a hint for minimize animations or similar effects.
The client is not required to set this geometry. If unset, the compositor applies an implementation-defined default. If the client sets multiple rectangles, only the last one takes effect.
Coordinates are in surface-local space of the given surface. Setting width = height = 0 removes a previously set geometry.
The compositor raises the invalid_geometry error if the provided dimensions are otherwise out of range.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: surface that contains the visual representation

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x offset in surface-local coordinates

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y offset in surface-local coordinates

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the rectangle in surface-local coordinates

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the rectangle in surface-local coordinates

event.name: pid

description.summary: process ID of the owning application

event.description: Emitted by the compositor when it knows the process ID of the application that owns this toplevel. This event is sent once as part of the initial property snapshot, before the first done event, and is not re-sent unless the owning process changes.

arg.name: pid
arg.summary: process ID of the application

event.name: title

description.summary: toplevel title has changed

event.description: Emitted whenever the title of the toplevel changes. The initial title is sent as part of the snapshot before the first done event.

arg.name: title
arg.summary: the current title of the toplevel

event.name: app_id

description.summary: toplevel app-id has changed

event.description: Emitted whenever the app-id of the toplevel changes. The initial app-id is sent as part of the snapshot before the first done event.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: the current application ID of the toplevel

event.name: identifier

description.summary: a stable identifier for a toplevel

event.description:
This identifier is used to check if two or more toplevel handles belong to the same toplevel.
The identifier is useful for command line tools or privileged clients which may need to reference an exact toplevel across processes or instances of the treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2 global.
The compositor sends this event exactly once, when the handle is created, as part of the initial property snapshot.
The identifier must be unique per toplevel and its handles. Two different toplevels must not have the same identifier. The identifier is only valid as long as the toplevel is mapped. If the toplevel is unmapped the identifier must not be reused. An identifier must not be reused by the compositor to ensure there are no races when sharing identifiers between processes.

arg.name: identifier
arg.summary: unique stable identifier for this toplevel

event.name: output_enter

description.summary: toplevel is now visible on an output

event.description: Emitted when the toplevel becomes visible on the given output. A toplevel may be visible on multiple outputs simultaneously. This event is sent as part of the initial snapshot and whenever the set of visible outputs changes.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output the toplevel entered

event.name: output_leave

description.summary: toplevel is no longer visible on an output

event.description: Emitted when the toplevel stops being visible on the given output. A corresponding output_enter event for the same output is guaranteed to have been sent before this event.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output the toplevel left

event.name: state

description.summary: toplevel state has changed

event.description:
Emitted immediately after the handle is created as part of the initial property snapshot, and again each time the toplevel state changes due to a compositor action or a client request on this protocol.
The state argument is an array of uint32 values, each corresponding to an entry in the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2.state enum. An entry is present in the array when the corresponding state is active.

arg.name: state
arg.summary: array of active treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2.state enum values encoded as uint32

event.name: done

description.summary: all pending property changes have been sent

event.description:
Emitted after the compositor has sent all property events for the current atomic update batch (title, app_id, pid, identifier, state, output_enter, output_leave, parent). The client should process the preceding events as a single coherent state snapshot only upon receiving done.
This allows changes to the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 properties to be atomically applied. Other protocols which extend the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 interface may use this event to also atomically apply any pending state.
This event must not be sent after the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2.closed event.

event.name: closed

description.summary: the toplevel window has been unmapped

event.description:
Emitted when the toplevel is unmapped or destroyed by the compositor. No further property events will be sent on this handle after closed. The handle becomes inert; the client must not send any requests except destroy, which it should call promptly to release compositor-side tracking resources.
Other protocols which extend the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2 interface must also ignore requests other than their destructors.

event.name: parent

description.summary: parent toplevel has changed

event.description:
Emitted whenever the parent-child relationship of this toplevel changes. The parent arg is null when the toplevel has no parent (i.e. it is a top-level root window).
This event is not re-sent when the client destroys the parent handle; the relationship on the compositor side is unchanged by client-side destruction of the parent object.

arg.name: parent
arg.summary: the parent toplevel handle, or null if there is no parent

interface.name: treeland_dock_preview_context_v2

description.summary: dock preview and tooltip context for a surface

interface.description:
Provides the dock or taskbar component with the ability to display a thumbnail preview of one or more toplevels and to show tooltip overlays, both positioned relative to the anchor surface supplied to get_dock_preview_context.
The object is created by treeland_foreign_toplevel_manager_v2.get_dock_preview_context and is valid until the client calls destroy. The compositor emits enter and leave events when the pointer enters or leaves the active preview area.

enum.name: direction

description.summary: position of the preview relative to the anchor surface

enum.description: Specifies on which side of the anchor surface the preview popup or tooltip should appear. The compositor uses this value as a placement hint; it may choose a different side if the requested side would be clipped by the screen edge.

entry.name: top
entry.summary: preview appears above the anchor surface

entry.name: right
entry.summary: preview appears to the right of the anchor surface

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: preview appears below the anchor surface

entry.name: left
entry.summary: preview appears to the left of the anchor surface

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the dock preview context

request.description: Destroy the treeland_dock_preview_context_v2 object and release all associated compositor resources. Any visible preview or tooltip is hidden immediately. After this request the compositor will no longer send any event.

request.name: show

description.summary: show a thumbnail preview of the given toplevels

request.description:
Request that the compositor display thumbnail previews for the toplevels identified by the identifiers array. The popup is positioned at (x, y) in the coordinate space of the anchor surface supplied at context creation, on the side indicated by direction.
The identifiers argument is a wl_array of uint32 identifier values, each matching the identifier sent by the treeland_foreign_toplevel_handle_v2.identifier event. The compositor ignores identifiers that do not correspond to a currently mapped toplevel.
Calling show while a preview is already visible replaces the previous content atomically.

arg.name: identifiers
arg.summary: array of uint32 toplevel identifiers to preview

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y offset of the preview popup in anchor-surface-local coordinates

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: which side of the anchor surface the preview appears on

request.name: show_tooltip

description.summary: show a tooltip near the anchor surface

request.description:
Request that the compositor display a text tooltip at (x, y) in the coordinate space of the anchor surface, on the side indicated by direction. Any previously visible tooltip from this context is replaced.
Calling show_tooltip while a preview is visible does not hide the preview; both may be visible simultaneously depending on compositor policy.

arg.name: tooltip
arg.summary: UTF-8 text to display in the tooltip

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x offset of the tooltip in anchor-surface-local coordinates

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y offset of the tooltip in anchor-surface-local coordinates

arg.name: direction
arg.summary: which side of the anchor surface the tooltip appears on

request.name: close

description.summary: hide the preview popup

request.description: Request that the compositor hide the currently visible preview popup. If no preview is visible this request is a no-op. The tooltip, if any, is not affected.

event.name: enter

description.summary: pointer entered the preview area

event.description: Emitted when the pointer device enters the active preview popup area managed by this context. The compositor sends this event only while a preview is visible (i.e. after show and before close or destroy).

event.name: leave

description.summary: pointer left the preview area

event.description: Emitted when the pointer device leaves the active preview popup area managed by this context. A corresponding enter event is guaranteed to have been sent before this event.
